title.en: Explain six factors affecting price determination
Use the break-even idea to see the cost floor of price

say.en: Price is the only P that brings in money. Cost, demand, competition and law all pull it in different directions. In this lesson: Define price.
Explain six factors affecting price determination.
Use the break-even idea to see the cost floor of price.

body.en: *Price* is the amount of money paid by buyers in exchange for a product or service. Factors affecting price: product cost (fixed, variable and semi-variable costs set the lower limit), utility and demand (the upper limit is what buyers are willing to pay), extent of competition, government and legal regulations, pricing objectives (profit maximisation, market share, facing competition, product quality leadership), and the marketing methods used.
body.kn: ಬೆಲೆ ಎಂದರೆ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನದ ವಿನಿಮಯಕ್ಕೆ ಖರೀದಿದಾರ ಕೊಡುವ ಹಣ. ಉತ್ಪನ್ನದ ವೆಚ್ಚ, ಉಪಯುಕ್ತತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಬೇಡಿಕೆ, ಸ್ಪರ್ಧೆ, ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ನಿಯಮಗಳು, ಬೆಲೆ ಉದ್ದೇಶಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಮಾರಾಟ ವಿಧಾನಗಳು ಬೆಲೆಯ ಮೇಲೆ ಪ್ರಭಾವ ಬೀರುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: In the long run, price must cover the total cost. The volume at which total revenue equals total cost is the *break-even* point: $\text{BEP} = \frac{\text{Fixed cost}}{\text{Price} - \text{Variable cost per unit}}$. A higher price lowers the break-even volume but may reduce demand.

problem.en: A firm making steel water bottles has fixed costs of ₹2,00,000 a year and a variable cost of ₹30 per bottle. How many bottles must it sell to break even at a price of ₹50? At ₹70?

steps.en: At ₹50: contribution per bottle = 50 − 30 = ₹20; BEP = 2,00,000 ÷ 20 = 10,000 bottles.
A higher price halves the break-even volume, but demand at ₹70 may be lower: cost and demand must both be considered.

narration.en: Let us work through this case together. A firm making steel water bottles has fixed costs of ₹2,00,000 a year and a variable cost of ₹30 per bottle. How many bottles must it sell to break even at a price of ₹50? At ₹70?

say.en: Let us work through this case together. A firm making steel water bottles has fixed costs of 2,00,000 rupees a year and a variable cost of 30 rupees per bottle. How many bottles must it sell to break even at a price of 50 rupees? At 70 rupees?
At 50 rupees: contribution per bottle equals 50 minus 30 equals 20 rupees; BEP equals 2,00,000 divided by 20 equals 10,000 bottles.
At 70 rupees: contribution equals 70 minus 30 equals 40 rupees; BEP equals 2,00,000 divided by 40 equals 5,000 bottles.
A higher price halves the break-even volume, but demand at 70 rupees may be lower: cost and demand must both be considered.
So the answer is 10,000 bottles at 50 rupees; 5,000 bottles at 70 rupees.

say.en: Competition, law, objectives and marketing methods also matter.
say.kn: ಸ್ಪರ್ಧೆ, ಕಾನೂನು, ಉದ್ದೇಶಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಮಾರಾಟ ವಿಧಾನಗಳೂ ಮುಖ್ಯ.

say.en: Break-even: fixed cost divided by (price - variable cost).
say.kn: ಸಮತೋಲನ ಬಿಂದು: ಸ್ಥಿರ ವೆಚ್ಚ divided by (ಬೆಲೆ - ಬದಲಾಗುವ ವೆಚ್ಚ).

say.en: Next: Place mix: channels and physical distribution.
say.kn: ಮುಂದೆ: ಸ್ಥಳ ಮಿಶ್ರಣ: ವಿತರಣಾ ಮಾರ್ಗಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಭೌತಿಕ ವಿತರಣೆ.
